title: The integral closure of a domain in a finite extension of its fraction field is a normal domain with that fraction field
statement: Let $A$ be an integral domain with fraction field $F$, let $L/F$ be a finite field extension, and let $A'\subseteq L$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ (the elements of $L$ satisfying a monic polynomial with coefficients in $A$). Then $A'$ is an integral domain, $L$ is a fraction field of $A'$ (the inclusion $A'\subseteq L$ extends to an isomorphism $\operatorname{Frac}(A')\xrightarrow{\sim}L$), and $A'$ is integrally closed in $L$, i.e. $A'$ is a normal domain.
